description: Participants design randomised experiments for a fictional municipal permits office and read the results without fooling themselves. They turn a decision question into a pre-registration with a hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, a stop rule and a unit of randomisation, compute sample size by formula and by simulation, analyse a synthetic experiment log, check that randomisation worked, and measure how peeking, many metrics and a mismatched unit inflate false wins. Variance reduction and sequential tests are left to DS-302.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: Computes a proportion, a difference in means and a confidence interval
Writes a simulation loop in Python or R

outcomes.text: Distinguish a randomised experiment, a quasi-experiment and an observational comparison, and explain the causal claim each supports, given six study descriptions from public services
outcomes.evidence: a classification with the supported claim, at least five of six correct

outcomes.text: Draft a pre-registration stating the decision, hypothesis, unit of randomisation, primary and guardrail metrics, stop rule and analysis plan, given the office's question about renewal reminders
outcomes.evidence: a one-page pre-registration that passes a reviewer's checklist

outcomes.text: Compute the sample size and run time needed to detect a minimum effect of interest and check it by simulation, given baseline renewal rates, daily traffic and the office's minimum effect
outcomes.evidence: a notebook with the formula result, a simulated power curve and the chosen duration

outcomes.text: Analyse a completed two-arm experiment with a difference in proportions, a confidence interval and a sample ratio mismatch test, given a synthetic log of 60,000 renewal notices
outcomes.evidence: a result note with estimate, interval, checks and a recommendation

outcomes.text: Measure by simulation the false-positive rate caused by peeking, many metrics and analysis at the wrong unit, given simulated A/A tests with no true effect
outcomes.evidence: a table of false-win rates for each trap, with and without the correct procedure

outcomes.text: Review a reported experiment and decide whether it supports the decision it claims to support, given write-ups with seeded flaws, one in class and one in the capstone
outcomes.evidence: a review memo per write-up naming each flaw, its consequence and the decision the evidence does support, defended live
